I went full circle around it both days and I was very surprised with the amount of old bottles, broken glass and other trash I pulled from it. Some vintage bottles I have never seen before as well. 
Big thanks to Owen Keough and also to Dallas Smith. Both followers to my page who reached out and offered to cover my expenses on this combined 2 day big cleanup. 
Your kindness is greatly appreciated and this pond is much healthier and safer because you both care. 
Stay safe and enjoy the great outdoors:)

I pulled this 1 litre bottle off bottom in Paddys pond yesterday. It was standing upright in the mud and full of motor oil. It has been there for awhile and I’m very thankful that the plastic didn’t break down and the oil leak out. 
One litre of oil can contaminate one million litres of water which is terrible for the fish, frogs, insects, birds, etc. 
Toxic poisoning and it reduces the oxygen levels as it creates a thin film over the surface which blocks sunlight and stops oxygen from moving between air and water. 
This bottle of oil will go to a used oil drop off location to be recycled. Water is life! Stay safe:)

Here’s a feel good story for all to read. It’s called “ Pop’s Pond “ 
A couple days ago we did a cleanup of one section of Four Mile Pond and found some interesting items including some vintage bottles near the TCH on the bottom of this beautiful waterbody. Our FB post got shared to Wanda Murphy-O’Rielly who reached out to us with her nostalgic and touching story. 
She tells us of how Four Mile Pond is very special to her and her family as her late grandfather, Frank Rickert, who passed away almost 31 years ago had built a cabin near where we had conducted the cleanup. 
Wanda’s mom, now 78 year old Irene Murphy, was just 8 years old when Frank came home one day and said he had bought this piece of land and was going to build a cabin, and so he did. 
This little piece of heaven, the cabin, was a place where Wanda and family spent a lot  of time over the years berry picking, fishing, hunting, exploring and swimming. “It’s where they all learned how to swim, “she says. She recalls having many jiggs dinners cooked in the water from the pond. Her grandparents had 8 children and 19 grandchildren so you can imagine the feeds, the stories and the fun times there. Even after the fun ended and it was time to pack up and head home they would all take baths in the pond, which was not at all uncommon back in the day. 
Eventually with the new highway developments the cabin was taken down to make room for the divided highways and ramps. A lot of fond memories in “ Pops pond “ as they would all refer to it. 
Wanda, who shares the same birthday as her pop which makes it even more special to her , thanked us for our efforts in cleaning everything up from the pond bottom and asked what we were going to do with all the items, as she was interested in just one thing, one item from a time she holds so dear. 
We never hesitated and were more than happy to make her day when we told her to drop over and pick up a Vintage embossed glass Javex bottle that we pulled off the bottom near to where her pops cabin was built. Quite possible it was once in the hands of her pop, Frank Rickert, so many years ago. 
May you and your mom, Irene enjoy this treasure for many years to come. Myself ( Lou) and Jay are delighted the vintage bottle found its home on your mantle and you can see it often to reflect and remember the wonderful memories of your childhood at “ Pop’s Pond.”

Spent the day hiking the hillsides near Riverhead, NL moose hunting . Every side trail I took that led me further back into the country I would bring a pile of recyclables out on my way back that I found tossed in the trees . People have no respect for nature! Some of the items I could not take are , hot water tank , microwave, steel door, barbecue, 3 toilets , bathroom sink, vehicle and ATV tires, radio , 45 gallon drums , 2 gill nets , vinyl  siding , roof shingles, plastic lawn  chairs , etc . Litter degrades natural areas, kills plants and animals and pollutes our waters.  We have recycling programs and landfill / waste management sites . Totally unacceptable and unfair to the ones that enjoy the outdoors , our kids and grandkids coming after us and all the animals , birds and fish .
